title: Pico World Race

scout.reason: Quality has substantial public play support, and source availability makes local construction credible. The repository supplies cartridge files; source exposes RaceState, PlayerLap, TokenCollected, RaceCompletePos and RaceCompleteTime, plus InitRace and restart/retry paths. These are promising instrumentation points, not a verified browser API. The material uncertainty is whether the current hosted build starts and controls correctly; offline boot, fresh-save access and task durations were not tested.
evidence: The [creator's page](https://pak-9.itch.io/pico-world-race) was retrievable and links a browser iframe. It documents keyboard steering, Z acceleration and X brake/drift.

The [playable iframe](https://html-classic.itch.zone/html/6362442/index.html) yielded no usable gameplay through the web tool; direct shell requests failed DNS resolution. No title screen or controllable race was observed.
ideas: Complete one lap of USA from a fresh race start.
Finish a USA race having collected at least 10 of its 20 tokens.

builder.summary: A robust offline environment is feasible. The official export boots offline, accepts held keyboard input, and supports a small GPIO hook exposing meaningful gameplay state. Cache-only experiments verified five unlocked track starts and repeatable initialization. No tracked files were edited.
Packaged the offline runtime, readable game_api.js, player guide and all eight frozen tasks. Focused checks passed; ready for EVALUATE.
Offline play, player controls, all eight task contracts and two resets verified. Final-event checks used cache-only checkpoints. Shipped files remained unchanged.

vlm_report.43_07: The game screen remains frozen on the same distorted off-track frame at 10 MPH after repeated throttle and steering inputs, and I expected the car to move or recover; every attempted control has no visible effect.

vlm_repair.summary: The freeze report does not hold up: original video and gameplay state change during the reported inputs. This is the model's own failure; no repair is proposed. Offline play, all eight task starts, and two resets work. Runtime, guide, and task definitions remain unchanged.
No changes warranted: the freeze report is the model's own failure. Preserved the runtime, guide, and all eight frozen task contracts. Ready for EVALUATE.

The freeze report is the model's own failure: recorded inputs changed both gameplay state and frames. All eight task contracts, documented controls, offline starts, and resets verified. Completion checks used cache-only native-event checkpoints. Runtime, guide, and tasks remain unchanged.

policy_request.summary: Pico World Race is playable offline and supports the requested observation extension. No runtime, catalog, task, or gameAPI changes were made. None of the five requested fields is already reliably readable from the page. All five are feasible for engine_hook publication: player_motion from native momentum, airborne height and recovery state; visible_road from renderer-visible geometry; visible_tokens from rendered uncollected tokens; visible_opponents from rendered cars and their current velocities; visible_obstacles from rendered collidable scenery and projected rectangles. Publication remains for IMPLEMENT, with viewport and hill-occlusion filtering required. Preserve all eight existing tasks and the existing GPIO/gameAPI contract.

Published all five requested fields through window.__policyObservation.getState() in game_api.js: player_motion, visible_road, visible_tokens, visible_opponents and visible_obstacles. All use engine_hook provenance; none were already readable or omitted. Fields return null before a racing frame exists. Existing gameAPI bytes, tasks, catalog and controls remain unchanged. Ready for independent EVALUATE.

Published and verified all five requested fields: player_motion, visible_road, visible_tokens, visible_opponents and visible_obstacles. All use engine_hook provenance; none were already readable or omitted. The bridge returns exactly five JSON keys, handles startup and resets, and keeps observations separate from gameAPI. All eight frozen task contracts passed evaluation. No runtime, catalog or task files changed during EVALUATE.
